title: Farol Protocol v0.1 — JSON-RPC Error Object
description:
The `error` member of any Farol protocol JSON-RPC response (handshake/hello, widget/get, action/invoke). See protocol/SPEC.md §8 for the normative prose. `code` follows the standard JSON-RPC 2.0 reserved range (-32700..-32600..-32603) for generic protocol errors, or the Farol domain range (-32000 to -32099) for the reasons below. `data.reason` is REQUIRED whenever `code` is one of the Farol domain codes.

Farol domain error catalog (protocol v0.1, code -> reason -> where -> meaning):
-32000 -> protocol_version_incompatible -> handshake/hello response (plugin-side refusal path) -> the plugin refuses the protocol_version proposed by the core.
-32001 -> fetch_failed -> action/invoke response -> the underlying action execution failed (e.g. `git fetch` returned a non-zero exit code); `data.detail` MAY carry the underlying error output.
-32002 -> action_timeout -> synthesized by the core (not the plugin) when RPC_TIMEOUT_ACTION elapses on a single action/invoke call -> does not by itself mark the plugin connection unavailable.
-32003 -> exec_unavailable -> handshake/hello or action/invoke response -> an executable the plugin depends on for a declared capability (e.g. `exec`) is not available in the environment; the plugin reports this as a pointwise failure without exiting its own process.
-32004 -> scan_root_unreadable -> widget/get response -> a configured path the plugin needs to read exists but is not accessible (permission error) - distinct from "does not exist/empty", which MUST be reported as success with empty data, never as an error.

This catalog is normative for the git-local reference plugin. A future plugin MAY reserve additional `reason` values within the same -32000..-32099 code range, documented in that plugin's own section, as long as it does not reuse a `code` already defined above with a different meaning. `data.reason` is therefore intentionally left as an open string (not a closed enum) in this schema so that forward-compatible plugins are not rejected by validation.

ErrorObject.title: ErrorObject
ErrorObject.description: Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error object, as used by every Farol protocol method. `message` is for humans/logs only - code MUST distinguish error kinds via `code`/`data.reason`, never by parsing `message`.

code.description: Numeric error identifier. Either a standard JSON-RPC 2.0 reserved code (-32700, -32600, -32601, -32602, -32603) or a Farol domain code in the reserved application range -32000 to -32099 (see this file's top-level description for the v0.1 catalog).

message.description: Human-readable error message, for logs/diagnostics. Not a stable identifier - callers MUST use `code`/`data.reason` for programmatic handling.

data.description: Structured error detail. REQUIRED to be present with a `reason` field whenever `code` is a Farol domain code (-32000 to -32099). Additional properties beyond `reason` vary per `reason` (e.g. `detail`, `target`) and are intentionally left open by this schema.

reason.description: Farol domain reason string, e.g. "protocol_version_incompatible", "fetch_failed", "action_timeout", "exec_unavailable", "scan_root_unreadable", or a future plugin-specific reason within the reserved code range. Intentionally not a closed enum, to remain forward-compatible with reasons introduced by future plugins/versions.
